checked_sources.source: Kyoungseok Jang, Kwang-Sung Jun, Ilja Kuzborskij, Francesco Orabona, Tighter PAC-Bayes Bounds Through Coin-Betting, COLT 2023
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a time-uniform PAC-Bayes concentration inequality for independent observations whose parameter/posterior may depend on the observed sample. The main result holds simultaneously over all sample sizes and all data-dependent posteriors relative to a data-free prior, with a KL(P_n||P_0) complexity term. This directly supplies a statistical mechanism for paying for data-dependent search without forcing a fixed candidate chosen before all observations. The exact source setting is independent observations and posterior-averaged risk, not adaptive-logging off-policy deployment.

checked_sources.source: Benjamin Chugg, Hongjian Wang, Aaditya Ramdas, A Unified Recipe for Deriving (Time-Uniform) PAC-Bayes Bounds, JMLR 2023
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a supermartingale/mixture recipe for anytime-valid PAC-Bayes bounds across a broad class of stochastic processes, including non-i.i.d. and nonstationary settings. This broadens the route beyond the independent-observation specialization of the coin-betting result, while still requiring the chosen PAC-Bayes construction to match the actual data process and target quantity.

checked_sources.source: J. Jon Ryu, Gregory W. Wornell, Gambling-Based Confidence Sequences for Bounded Random Vectors, ICML 2024
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified joint time-uniform confidence sets for means of bounded random vectors using gambling/portfolio constructions. The vector formulation can exploit dependence among coordinates and is a direct candidate for monitoring utility plus several safety/calibration metrics jointly rather than treating each coordinate as an unrelated scalar test. It is a vector-mean inference primitive, not by itself an off-policy policy-selection theorem.

checked_sources.source: Niklas Werge et al., Weighted Sequential Bayesian Inference for Non-Stationary Linear Contextual Bandits, UAI 2026
checked_sources.result: Recent sequential contextual-bandit work includes time-uniform concentration for vector-valued martingales under nonstationarity, reinforcing that multi-dimensional sequential uncertainty control can coexist with adaptive decision data. Its exact objective is weighted Bayesian inference, not a ready-made multi-certificate deployment gate.

checked_sources.source: David Martinez-Taboada et al., Vector-valued self-normalized concentration inequalities beyond sub-Gaussianity, ALT 2026
checked_sources.result: Primary source extends vector-valued self-normalized concentration beyond sub-Gaussian assumptions using Bernstein/Bennett-style bounds, with applications to online regression and bandits. This is relevant if monitored certificate coordinates are light-tailed but not well modeled as sub-Gaussian.

candidates_new.mechanism: Place a data-free prior over a complexity-controlled policy/configuration family and maintain a data-dependent posterior over candidates as evidence arrives. Use a time-uniform PAC-Bayes confidence sequence so the posterior may be selected from the same data while the complexity cost is paid through KL(P_t||P_0). This is a route to same-stream adaptive candidate selection that is more flexible than a fixed finite candidate list and does not require a fresh holdout merely because the posterior is data-dependent.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Jang et al.'s main coin-betting PAC-Bayes result holds with probability at least 1-delta simultaneously for all sample sizes, all data-dependent posteriors, and all data-free priors in its independent-observation setting. The bound replaces a global class-capacity penalty by KL(P_n||P_0) and yields confidence sequences. Chugg et al. give a general supermartingale recipe for time-uniform PAC-Bayes bounds over broader stochastic processes.
candidates_new.scope: The coin-betting theorem directly covers independent observations and posterior-averaged bounded losses/means. The general recipe covers broader processes only when a valid supermartingale for the target quantity is available. Neither source directly proves adaptive-logging off-policy current-baseline deployment of one deterministic argmax policy with multiple safety constraints.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: A data-dependent prior built from the same evidence without a valid construction can invalidate the guarantee. Expanding the hypothesis space after seeing data is not free unless the original prior already covers it or a valid hierarchical/online PAC-Bayes treatment pays for it. Posterior-averaged certification does not automatically certify the single most-probable or argmax configuration. Importance weighting/coverage issues remain separate in off-policy use.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: An automation optimizer can keep probability mass over a broad predeclared configuration family and update that posterior from execution evidence, paying a KL search-complexity penalty rather than repeatedly creating uncorrected post-selection tests. Deployment should still pass through a current-baseline release certificate and pathwise invariant shield.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the source-domain time-uniform data-dependent-posterior principle; medium for off-policy automation transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Represent progress/utility and multiple safety/calibration quantities as a vector and maintain one joint time-uniform confidence region instead of independent scalar intervals with a naive alpha split. Release only when the entire confidence region lies inside the acceptable orthant: the utility coordinate is above the current-baseline requirement while every safety coordinate stays below its hard bound. Dependence among coordinates can potentially reduce conservatism compared with treating them independently.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Ryu & Wornell establish time-uniform confidence sets for bounded random-vector means using gambling strategies and report tighter sets than existing baselines in some simulations. The 2026 vector-martingale/self-normalized work broadens available sequential concentration tools beyond stationary scalar sub-Gaussian models. A direct sample-saving number versus Bonferroni scalar certificates for the intended multi-metric gate has not yet been primary-verified.
candidates_new.scope: Sequential inference on vector means/martingales under the assumptions of the chosen construction. The cited vector confidence sequences do not by themselves correct off-policy importance weighting, candidate-selection bias, or hard pathwise safety.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: High dimension or weak coordinate dependence can make a joint region expensive or no tighter than scalar methods. Mis-specified tail/boundedness assumptions invalidate calibration. Joint vector validity still needs a separate valid mapping from adaptively selected policy/configuration to observed vector outcomes.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Use one dependency-aware anytime certificate for utility plus contamination/scope/reliability metrics after candidate selection has been made statistically valid. This preserves non-compensating constraints while potentially avoiding unnecessary alpha fragmentation.
candidates_new.confidence: high for vector sequential inference; medium for sample-efficiency benefit in the automation gate

evidence_updates.update: The frontier is now partially resolved beyond fixed finite classes: time-uniform PAC-Bayes bounds can hold simultaneously across all sample sizes and data-dependent posteriors, so a same-stream selected randomized hypothesis/configuration distribution can be validly certified when it stays inside the prior-covered class and assumptions hold. What remains open is the direct off-policy adaptive-logging/current-baseline/vector-constraint deployment composition and deterministic-candidate extraction.

Joint bounded-vector confidence sequences provide a plausible less-conservative alternative to independent scalar alpha splitting for multiple certificate channels. No direct source yet quantifies the sample saving for the exact correlated utility+safety gate, so this remains a candidate mechanism rather than a measured improvement.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Time-uniform PAC-Bayes automatically certifies whichever single deterministic configuration has the highest posterior score.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established by the inspected source. The central PAC-Bayes object is posterior-averaged risk/mean; extracting one deterministic member can require an additional argument or a separate certificate.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Keep posterior-mixture versus deterministic deployment as an explicit frontier item.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A joint vector confidence sequence automatically solves adaptive candidate-selection and off-policy overlap problems.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: False. Vector concentration controls multiple coordinates of a valid stochastic process; it does not create support where none exists and does not remove post-selection bias unless the candidate-selection process is itself covered by a uniform/PAC-Bayes/online-learning construction.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Compose vector inference only after selection-validity and coverage gates.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Naive Bonferroni/alpha splitting is always substantially worse than a joint vector certificate.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not quantified for the intended correlated automation metrics in the inspected primary sources.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Retain as an empirical comparison frontier rather than claiming a universal advantage.

Quantify joint vector confidence-sequence sample cost versus Bonferroni or alpha-spending scalar certificates under positively and negatively correlated utility/safety metrics.

Search for vector-valued off-policy confidence sequences/e-processes that combine adaptive logging and multiple outcome constraints directly, rather than composing generic vector concentration with scalar OPE.
